original_question: Investigate the Krylov solvability of the inverse problem Af = g for the classical Friedrichs operator on a bounded Lipschitz domain Ω ⊂ R^d defined by Af = Σ_{k=1}^d ∂k(B_k f) + C f, where each coefficient matrix B_k lies in W^{1,∞}(Ω, M_r), each B_k is self-adjoint, and C lies in L^∞(Ω, M_r) with C + C* + Σ_{k=1}^d ∂k B_k > μ 1 almost everywhere for some μ > 0. The goal is to determine what assumptions on the coefficient matrices B_k and C lead to Krylov-solvable inverse problems of this Friedrichs type.
target_in_paper: Section 4, Question 4: the paper’s concrete open problem is to investigate the Krylov-solvability of the inverse problem induced by the classical Friedrichs operator (3.1), under suitable conditions on the coefficient matrix functions appearing in (3.1)–(3.2). This is the concrete counterpart of the preceding abstract questions, and it is the nearest official formulation to your draft. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2406.05777))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right target level of the paper: the classical Friedrichs operator on a bounded Lipschitz domain, with the same differential expression and coefficient hypotheses coming from Section 3, and the goal of studying Krylov solvability rather than a broader abstract Friedrichs-operator problem. In other words, you are aiming at Question 4, not at the more abstract Questions 1–3. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2406.05777))
missing_details: The paper states this as an investigation problem ('Question 4'), not as a request for a complete characterization theorem; wording such as 'investigate under suitable conditions' is closer to the paper than 'determine exactly all assumptions'. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2406.05777))

The draft does not define 'Krylov-solvable'. In the paper, for a solvable inverse problem Af = g, this means that there exists a solution f in the Hilbert-space closure of the Krylov subspace K(A,g) = span{g, Ag, A^2g, ...}. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2406.05777))

The draft omits the dependence on the chosen closed realization of the differential expression, equivalently on the boundary conditions at ∂Ω. Section 3 explicitly says that solvability and well-posedness for the classical Friedrichs operator depend on which realization is chosen. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2406.05777))

The draft does not quantify over the datum g or state that one is considering those g for which the realized problem Af = g is actually solvable. Without this, the phrase 'Krylov-solvable inverse problem' is underspecified. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2406.05777))

To be fully stand-alone, the question should name the operator A whose Krylov subspace is used: namely, a closed realization of the classical Friedrichs differential expression, not just the formal differential expression itself. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2406.05777))

The paper’s framework is Hilbert-space based, and the concrete Friedrichs problem is meant as a concrete instance of that Hilbert-space notion. The draft leaves this ambient setting implicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2406.05777))
refined_question: Let A be a closed realization, determined by boundary conditions on ∂Ω, of the classical Friedrichs differential expression A0f = Σ_{k=1}^d ∂k(Bk f) + C f on a bounded Lipschitz domain Ω ⊂ ℝ^d, where Bk ∈ W^{1,∞}(Ω, M_r(ℂ)), each Bk is self-adjoint a.e., C ∈ L^∞(Ω, M_r(ℂ)), and C + C* + Σ_{k=1}^d ∂kBk ≥ μ I_r a.e. for some μ > 0. For those data g for which the inverse problem Af = g is solvable, investigate which additional suitable conditions on the coefficients Bk and C, and on the chosen realization A (equivalently, on the boundary conditions), ensure that Af = g admits a Krylov solution, i.e. a solution f belonging to the closure of K(A,g) = span{g, Ag, A^2g, ...}. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2406.05777))
justification: This rewrite stays with the paper’s exact concrete target, namely Section 4, Question 4, instead of drifting to the broader abstract Questions 1–3. It also imports the hidden context from Section 3 that is necessary to make Question 4 stand alone: the classical Friedrichs operator is only a differential expression until one fixes a closed realization, and solvability depends on that choice of boundary conditions. Finally, Sections 1 and 2 supply the paper’s exact meaning of Krylov solvability via the closure of the Krylov subspace associated with A and g, which your draft assumed but did not state. The paper says that Question 4 mirrors the abstract questions at the concrete differential-operator level, but it does not explicitly prove an equivalent reformulation of Question 4, so no alternate equivalent formulation should be added. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2406.05777))
